questions.subject: Nigerian History
questions.learningObjective: Explain how mobilisation and negotiation contributed to constitutional change.
questions.prompt: Explain how the formation of trade unions could contribute to nationalist mobilisation in colonial Nigeria. Give one reason why evidence of a union’s existence alone would be insufficient to establish its contribution to a particular constitutional reform.
questions.answer: Unions could organise workers around shared grievances and support collective demands. Establishing a link to a specific reform requires evidence of what the union demanded, what it did and how decision makers responded.
questions.explanation: The answer must connect organisation with action and identify the further evidence needed to support a causal claim.

markingGuide.description: Explains a way unions could organise or mobilise workers.
Links collective demands or action to political pressure.
Identifies evidence needed to connect a union to a particular reform.

questions.subject: Nigerian History
questions.learningObjective: Explain how mobilisation and negotiation contributed to constitutional change.
questions.prompt: How could collaboration with nationalist groups outside Nigeria strengthen Nigerian campaigns for constitutional change? Explain one possible benefit and one limit of using such collaboration as evidence that a particular reform would occur.
questions.answer: Collaboration could spread information, provide support or share organising experience. It could strengthen a campaign while the outcome still depended on decisions and negotiations affecting Nigeria. A contact abroad alone does not establish that a reform had been agreed.
questions.explanation: Credit a clear mechanism for support and a limit on what it demonstrates about the constitutional outcome.

markingGuide.description: Identifies a possible form of cross-border collaboration.
Explains how it could strengthen campaigning.
Explains why the contact alone cannot establish an agreed reform.

questions.subject: Nigerian History
questions.learningObjective: Explain how mobilisation and negotiation contributed to constitutional change.
questions.prompt: A historian finds a nationalist programme combining cultural events with political discussion. Which interpretation best explains how the activities could support a common aim?
questions.answer: Cultural participation could build shared identification while political discussion connected it to demands for change.
questions.explanation: The interpretation explains a link between cultural awareness and political mobilisation.
options: Cultural events automatically transferred legislative authority to their organisers.
A political programme prevented participants from taking part in cultural activities.
Cultural participation could build shared identification while political discussion connected it to demands for change.
Public discussion established the date of independence without further decisions.

questions.subject: Nigerian History
questions.learningObjective: Explain how mobilisation and negotiation contributed to constitutional change.
questions.prompt: Why did the formation of political parties matter for nationalist participation in the constitutional institutions of the 1950s?
questions.answer: Parties could organise candidates and support for the electoral opportunities created by constitutional change.
questions.explanation: The answer links political organisation to participation in representative institutions.
options: Parties could organise candidates and support for the electoral opportunities created by constitutional change.
Parties replaced every regional institution immediately upon registration.
Party membership was equivalent to membership of the United Nations.
Creating a party ended all differences over the allocation of powers.

questions.subject: Nigerian History
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish the 1960 independence settlement from admission to the United Nations.
questions.prompt: United Nations records show a Security Council recommendation and a General Assembly decision concerning Nigeria on 7 October 1960. Explain what each body did and why the two records concern stages of one admission process.
questions.answer: The Council recommended admission. The Assembly considered the application and admitted Nigeria. The recommendation and decision belong to the membership process that followed Nigeria’s independence.
questions.explanation: The Assembly record explicitly refers to receiving the Council’s recommendation before deciding to admit Nigeria.

markingGuide.description: Explains the procedural relationship and places admission after independence.

questions.subject: Nigerian History
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish the 1960 independence settlement from admission to the United Nations.
questions.prompt: The UN Mandate Registry labels Nigeria’s admission resolution as published in 1961, while the resolution text ends with 7 October 1960. A learner uses the publication label as the admission date. Explain how to resolve this discrepancy.
questions.answer: Publication metadata and the date of the decision describe different events. The resolution’s decision date is 7 October 1960, which the UN Nigeria membership account corroborates. The 1961 publication label does not change the date of admission.
questions.explanation: The task distinguishes the date of a historical act from the date assigned to its publication.

markingGuide.description: Distinguishes publication metadata from decision dating.
Uses the 7 October 1960 date in the resolution.
Identifies the corroborating UN Nigeria account.

questions.subject: Nigerian History
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish the 1960 independence settlement from admission to the United Nations.
questions.prompt: Which statement about Security Council resolution 160 (1960) and General Assembly resolution 1492 (XV) best fits the UN records of Nigeria’s admission?
questions.answer: The Council recommended membership and the Assembly decided to admit Nigeria.
questions.explanation: The documents record complementary institutional actions in the admission process.
options: Both documents created Nigeria’s independence constitution.
The Council admitted Nigeria while the Assembly selected its first government.
The Assembly decided the borders of the three Nigerian regions.
The Council recommended membership and the Assembly decided to admit Nigeria.

questions.subject: Nigerian History
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish the 1960 independence settlement from admission to the United Nations.
questions.prompt: A museum display has one panel on the 1 October 1960 independence settlement and another on the UN action of 7 October. Which evidence would best help visitors understand the second panel’s institutional purpose?
questions.answer: The admission resolution’s reference to Nigeria’s application and the Council’s recommendation.
questions.explanation: Those references explain what the UN bodies were considering and deciding.
options: The number of modern UN offices operating in Nigeria.
The admission resolution’s reference to Nigeria’s application and the Council’s recommendation.
A current timetable for Nigerian school examinations.
A list of cultural festivals held many years after independence.
